notes: 20 independently authored AQA-style questions; not copied from, or attributed to, a specific examination year.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A string 0.84 m long vibrates at its third harmonic at 150 Hz, with both ends fixed. Calculate its wavelength and wave speed, and explain the boundary conditions.
markPoints: Three half-wavelengths occupy its length: 3λ/2=0.84 m.
Wavelength is 0.56 m.
Wave speed fλ=150×0.56=84 m s⁻¹.
Fixed ends have zero displacement and therefore form nodes.
questions.modelAnswer: Three half-wavelengths occupy its length: 3λ/2=0.84 m. Wavelength is 0.56 m. Wave speed fλ=150×0.56=84 m s⁻¹. Fixed ends have zero displacement and therefore form nodes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Two coherent slits separated by 0.36 mm illuminate a screen 2.4 m away using wavelength 550 nm. Calculate the fringe spacing. Explain why a varying phase difference destroys the stable fringe pattern.
markPoints: Use w=λD/s, with units converted to metres.
Fringe spacing is 3.67×10⁻³ m.
A stable pattern requires a constant relative phase.
Rapid phase variation makes bright and dark fringes shift and average out.
questions.modelAnswer: Use w=λD/s, with units converted to metres. Fringe spacing is 3.67×10⁻³ m. A stable pattern requires a constant relative phase. Rapid phase variation makes bright and dark fringes shift and average out.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A 6.0 kg crate slides down a 28° slope at steady speed. State the directions of all forces and calculate friction and normal reaction. Take g=9.81 m s⁻².
markPoints: Weight acts vertically downward; reaction is perpendicular and friction acts uphill.
Constant speed means net force along the slope is zero.
Friction is mg sin28°=27.6 N uphill.
Normal reaction is mg cos28°=52.0 N.
questions.modelAnswer: Weight acts vertically downward; reaction is perpendicular and friction acts uphill. Constant speed means net force along the slope is zero. Friction is mg sin28°=27.6 N uphill. Normal reaction is mg cos28°=52.0 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A wire 1.50 m long and 0.40 mm in diameter extends by 1.90 mm under 32.0 N, within its elastic range. Estimate its Young modulus and state the area calculation.
markPoints: Wire radius is 2.0×10⁻⁴ m.
Area πr²=1.257×10⁻⁷ m².
Young modulus E=FL/(AΔL).
questions.modelAnswer: Wire radius is 2.0×10⁻⁴ m. Area πr²=1.257×10⁻⁷ m². Young modulus E=FL/(AΔL). E≈2.01×10¹¹ Pa.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: The terminal pd of a cell is 1.51 V at 0.30 A and 1.33 V at 0.90 A. Calculate emf and internal resistance and explain why extra readings improve this practical.
markPoints: From V=ε−Ir, gradient ΔV/ΔI=−0.18/0.60=−0.30 Ω.
Internal resistance r=0.30 Ω, the negative gradient.
Multiple readings allow a best-fit straight line and reduce random uncertainty.
questions.modelAnswer: From V=ε−Ir, gradient ΔV/ΔI=−0.18/0.60=−0.30 Ω. Internal resistance r=0.30 Ω, the negative gradient. Emf ε=1.51+0.30×0.30=1.60 V. Multiple readings allow a best-fit straight line and reduce random uncertainty.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Explain why a filament lamp I–V curve becomes less steep at larger potential differences. Describe how an experiment could obtain data with both positive and negative voltage.
markPoints: Higher current heats the filament.
More lattice vibrations cause more electron scattering and higher resistance.
The graph gradient ΔI/ΔV becomes smaller as current increases.
Reverse the supply polarity and measure signed current and voltage.
questions.modelAnswer: Higher current heats the filament. More lattice vibrations cause more electron scattering and higher resistance. The graph gradient ΔI/ΔV becomes smaller as current increases. Reverse the supply polarity and measure signed current and voltage.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: An NTC thermistor is 8 kΩ at 20°C and is in series with a 4 kΩ resistor across 12 V. Output is across the fixed resistor. Calculate output at 20°C and predict its change when temperature rises.
markPoints: Total series resistance is 12 kΩ.
Potential divider gives 12×4/(8+4)=4.0 V.
An NTC thermistor loses resistance on heating.
Fixed resistor takes an increasing share of supply voltage; output rises.
questions.modelAnswer: Total series resistance is 12 kΩ. Potential divider gives 12×4/(8+4)=4.0 V. An NTC thermistor loses resistance on heating. Fixed resistor takes an increasing share of supply voltage; output rises.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A ball leaves a 19.6 m high platform horizontally at 14 m s⁻¹. Ignore air resistance; g=9.8 m s⁻². Calculate flight time and horizontal range, and justify constant horizontal speed.
markPoints: Vertical drop: 19.6=½gt².
Flight time is 2.00 s.
Horizontal range is 14×2=28.0 m.
With negligible drag there is no horizontal force, hence zero horizontal acceleration.
questions.modelAnswer: Vertical drop: 19.6=½gt². Flight time is 2.00 s. Horizontal range is 14×2=28.0 m. With negligible drag there is no horizontal force, hence zero horizontal acceleration.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A motor forces a spring–mass oscillator at adjustable frequency. Explain the expected amplitude response as frequency increases through resonance, and describe how stronger damping changes its graph.
markPoints: Energy transfer to the oscillator is greatest near its natural frequency.
The amplitude peaks near resonance then falls away.
Damping transfers oscillation energy to surrounding systems.
Stronger damping reduces and broadens the resonance peak.
questions.modelAnswer: Energy transfer to the oscillator is greatest near its natural frequency. The amplitude peaks near resonance then falls away. Damping transfers oscillation energy to surrounding systems. Stronger damping reduces and broadens the resonance peak.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Measured times for ten oscillations are 14.6, 14.5, 14.7, 14.5, 14.8 and 14.5 s. Calculate the mean period and half-range uncertainty in the ten-period timing, and explain the advantage of timing ten periods.
markPoints: Mean of ten-period times is 14.6 s.
Mean period is 1.46 s.
Half-range is (14.8−14.5)/2=0.15 s for ten periods.
Longer total timing reduces the percentage influence of reaction-time error.
questions.modelAnswer: Mean of ten-period times is 14.6 s. Mean period is 1.46 s. Half-range is (14.8−14.5)/2=0.15 s for ten periods. Longer total timing reduces the percentage influence of reaction-time error.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Two equal opposite tangential forces of 18 N act at separated points on a steering wheel. Their parallel lines of action are 0.42 m apart. Find the couple moment and explain the zero net force.
markPoints: A couple's moment equals one force times perpendicular separation.
Moment is 18×0.42=7.56 N m.
Equal opposite forces cancel, so resultant force is zero.
Different lines of action still produce a non-zero turning effect.
questions.modelAnswer: A couple's moment equals one force times perpendicular separation. Moment is 18×0.42=7.56 N m. Equal opposite forces cancel, so resultant force is zero. Different lines of action still produce a non-zero turning effect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A pump raises 360 kg of water vertically by 7.5 m in 45 s. Its electrical input is 950 W. Calculate useful power and efficiency, using g=9.81 m s⁻².
markPoints: Useful energy gain mgh=26,487 J.
Useful power is 26,487/45=589 W.
Efficiency = useful power/input power.
Efficiency is about 589/950=0.620 or 62.0%.
questions.modelAnswer: Useful energy gain mgh=26,487 J. Useful power is 26,487/45=589 W. Efficiency = useful power/input power. Efficiency is about 589/950=0.620 or 62.0%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A 0.75 kg object follows a horizontal circle of radius 0.65 m at 2.4 revolutions each second. Calculate angular speed, centripetal acceleration and force; describe acceleration direction.
markPoints: Angular speed ω=2πf=15.08 rad s⁻¹.
Acceleration a=ω²r≈147.8 m s⁻².
Centripetal force F=ma≈111 N.
Acceleration points toward the centre because the velocity direction changes.
questions.modelAnswer: Angular speed ω=2πf=15.08 rad s⁻¹. Acceleration a=ω²r≈147.8 m s⁻². Centripetal force F=ma≈111 N. Acceleration points toward the centre because the velocity direction changes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Light of wavelength 610 nm passes through a 0.12 mm slit. Using sinθ≈λ/a for the first minimum, calculate θ in degrees and predict the width of the central maximum if slit width halves.
markPoints: Halving a approximately doubles θ and broadens the central maximum.
questions.modelAnswer: Use λ=6.10×10⁻⁷ m and a=1.20×10⁻⁴ m. sinθ=0.005083. θ≈0.291°. Halving a approximately doubles θ and broadens the central maximum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Explain why a fibre-optic endoscope has a core and cladding of different refractive indices. Describe why image fibres are arranged coherently and why illumination often needs a separate bundle.
markPoints: Core refractive index is greater than cladding's.
Suitable rays are guided through total internal reflection.
A coherent bundle keeps neighbouring fibres in the same relative positions, preserving the image.
Illumination fibres carry light to the observed region.
questions.modelAnswer: Core refractive index is greater than cladding's. Suitable rays are guided through total internal reflection. A coherent bundle keeps neighbouring fibres in the same relative positions, preserving the image. Illumination fibres carry light to the observed region.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A 120-turn coil's flux per turn changes from 3.0 mWb to −1.0 mWb uniformly in 0.080 s. Find the magnitude of induced emf and explain Lenz's law in this case.
markPoints: Magnitude of flux change per turn is 4.0×10⁻³ Wb.
Change in flux linkage is 120×0.004=0.48 Wb turns.
Induced emf magnitude is 0.48/0.080=6.0 V.
The induced current produces an effect opposing the change in flux, not merely the existing field.
questions.modelAnswer: Magnitude of flux change per turn is 4.0×10⁻³ Wb. Change in flux linkage is 120×0.004=0.48 Wb turns. Induced emf magnitude is 0.48/0.080=6.0 V. The induced current produces an effect opposing the change in flux, not merely the existing field.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A 0.18 m wire carries 3.5 A perpendicular to a 0.42 T field. Find its magnetic force, and the force when it makes an angle of 30° with the field.
markPoints: Apply F=BILsinθ.
At 30° sinθ=0.5.
New force is about 0.132 N.
questions.modelAnswer: Apply F=BILsinθ. At 90° F=0.42×3.5×0.18=0.265 N. At 30° sinθ=0.5. New force is about 0.132 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: An electron transition releases 3.2 eV. Calculate the photon energy in joules and frequency, given e=1.60×10⁻¹⁹ C and h=6.63×10⁻³⁴ J s. Explain line spectra.
markPoints: Use E=hf.
Quantised energy levels restrict transitions to specific photon frequencies.
questions.modelAnswer: E=3.2×1.60×10⁻¹⁹=5.12×10⁻¹⁹ J. Use E=hf. f≈7.72×10¹⁴ Hz. Quantised energy levels restrict transitions to specific photon frequencies.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A 0.20 kg trolley at 3.6 m s⁻¹ sticks to a stationary 0.40 kg trolley on a smooth track. Calculate their shared speed and kinetic energy lost.
markPoints: Momentum before equals after: 0.20×3.6=0.60v.
Shared speed v=1.20 m s⁻¹.
Initial KE=1.296 J and final KE=0.432 J.
KE lost=0.864 J, despite conservation of momentum.
questions.modelAnswer: Momentum before equals after: 0.20×3.6=0.60v. Shared speed v=1.20 m s⁻¹. Initial KE=1.296 J and final KE=0.432 J. KE lost=0.864 J, despite conservation of momentum.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A 0.0480 m card passes through a light gate in 9.60 ms. Find the speed estimate. Explain why this isn't an exact instantaneous speed, and identify one measurement uncertainty.
markPoints: Passage time is 0.00960 s.
Estimated speed is 0.0480/0.00960=5.00 m s⁻¹.
This is an average over the finite length of card.
Card-length measurement or gate timing introduces uncertainty.
questions.modelAnswer: Passage time is 0.00960 s. Estimated speed is 0.0480/0.00960=5.00 m s⁻¹. This is an average over the finite length of card. Card-length measurement or gate timing introduces uncertainty.
